subject: Hosted API traffic slab & $/1M targets — follow-up and pricing scenarios
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood-inference.com>
To: Alex Bennett <alex.bennett@lynkhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API traffic slab & $/1M targets — follow-up and pricing scenarios

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap + a few asks so we can lock in a pricing proposal that matches LynkHealth's economics. I captured the traffic profile you shared and attached a simple token_profile.csv with the per-endpoint breakdown. Please confirm the two items below so we can price accurately: 

1) Monthly steady-state token range (total across endpoints): you said ~10–20M; can you confirm a tighter band (e.g., 12–16M)?
2) Peak concurrency / TPS during day-part peaks: you mentioned bursts around midday — can you confirm expected peak TPS for generation requests (approx tokens/sec or requests/sec with avg tokens per request)?

Based on our quick estimates we generally see 3 pricing levers that matter for you: committed monthly volume (discount), peak TPS/burst capacity (influences whether Dedicated or hosted burst is needed), and target $/1M tokens you want to hit for budget planning. If you can confirm the two items above we'll send 3 concrete scenarios (baseline, committed, and committed+burst) with per-1M pricing and monthly totals.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the tighter monthly band + peak TPS (reply inline)
- We return a short table with 3 scenarios + recommended SLA/commit level by EOD tomorrow
- If a scenario looks good, Marissa will draft a term sheet and we can kick off procurement

Attachments: token_profile.csv (attachment stub)

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Bennett <alex.bennett@lynkhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 12:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Hosted API traffic slab & $/1M targets — follow-up and pricing scenarios

Neha — thanks for the recap and for walking through the architecture earlier. Confirming the numbers we discussed: 

- Monthly tokens: current conservative expectation is ~15,000,000 tokens/month (we've seen seasonal variance but that is our planning baseline).
- Peak: during our highest-volume windows we need ~55 TPS for generation requests (this assumes ~270 tokens per request on average). We can accept brief spikes up to ~70 TPS for under 10 minutes if needed.
- Target $/1M: finance is aiming for ~$20 per 1M tokens as a target to hit our FY28 budget. If you have a committed plan that gets us closer to $15–18/1M we can push for a longer-term commit.

We prefer a hosted API model for the speed of integration; if you think Dedicated is required for reliability versus cost trade-offs please flag it in the scenarios. We can also share a short anonymized traffic dump if helpful.

Thanks — I copied procurement for visibility.

Best,
Alex Bennett
Director, Product Operations

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood-inference.com>
To: Alex Bennett <alex.bennett@lynkhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API traffic slab & $/1M targets — follow-up and pricing scenarios

Alex — perfect, thanks for the clear numbers. Based on 15M/mo and 55 TPS peak (occasional 70 TPS spikes) here are three hosted pricing scenarios (all $ per 1M tokens). I included the monthly spend math so you can compare to your $/1M target. I've attached a short PDF summary.

Scenario A — Pay-as-you-go (no commit):
- List price: $28 / 1M tokens
- Estimated monthly spend at 15M: $420 (15 * $28)
- Peak handling: hosted autoscaling; no dedicated capacity reserved — spikes handled subject to burst limits
- Notes: easiest to start, no term commitment, unit cost higher

Scenario B — 6-month commit (recommended starter commit):
- Commit: 12M tokens/month for 6 months with monthly true-up
- Discounted price on committed units: $18 / 1M
- Overage price: $24 / 1M on consumption above commit
- Effective cost @ expected 15M (12M at $18 + 3M at $24): $ (12*18 + 3*24) = $ (216 + 72) = $288 -> $19.2 / 1M effective
- Peak handling: included within hosted burst policy; we recommend a modest burst add-on for predictable 70 TPS spikes ($500/month additional)

Scenario C — 12-month commit + burst reserve (best unit economics):
- Commit: 15M tokens/month for 12 months
- Price on committed units: $14 / 1M
- Overage price: $20 / 1M
- Effective cost @ expected 15M: $210 (15*14) -> $14 / 1M
- Includes 70 TPS burst reserve for short windows (no per-minute surcharge up to configured burst capacity)
- Notes: requires longer-term commitment but hits your target band ($15–18) and reduces unit variability

Quick recommendation from us: Scenario B is a practical near-term win (meets finance target ~ $19.2/1M, low bar for commit). Scenario C is the only way to reliably hit $14–15/1M. If procurement is OK with a 12-month commit we can lock Scenario C and include a monthly burst reserve. 

Next steps:
- Please confirm whether Scenario B or C is preferable (or request an alternate commit size)
- If C, we'll produce a term sheet + PO template and Marissa will pick up contracting
- If B, we can prepare a 6-month SOW and draft the billing annex

Attachments: slab_pricing_estimate.pdf (attachment stub)

Thanks and happy to hop on a quick 20-min call to walk the math with finance if that helps.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
